families.name: Block sensitivity separation
families.statement: The quantity is the exponent \(\alpha\) in \(\mathrm{bs}(f)\ge s(f)^{\alpha-o(1)}\), for a family of total Boolean functions \(f\) with \(s(f)\to\infty\). A higher exponent is better. The sensitivity \(s(f)\) is the largest number of single bits that change the value of \(f\) when flipped at one input. The block sensitivity \(\mathrm{bs}(f)\) is the largest number of disjoint sets of bits that each change the value of \(f\) when flipped at one input. Rubinstein’s 1995 construction gives \(\alpha=2\). Huang’s 2019 theorem, with Tal’s refinement, gives \(\mathrm{bs}(f)\le s(f)^4\), so \(\alpha\le4\). The OpenAI baseline builds one seed function \(f\) with \(s(f)\le A\) and block sensitivity \(\mathrm{bs}(f,0)\ge B\) at the all-zero input, and composes it with itself, which gives \(\alpha=\log B/\log A\). OpenAI’s Lean proof uses the seed with recursion depth \(d=9\) and size parameter \(M=9^{10}\).

families.name: Spin-one Haldane gap
families.statement: The quantity is the uniform periodic spin-one spectral-gap lower bound \(\gamma_L\) at \(J=1\), compared on the original domain of even \(L\ge2304\). A higher lower bound is better. The claim assumes the cited OpenAI spatial-transfer identities and certified finite inputs. The extension to every integer \(L\ge24\) is listed under Relevant repos.
